name: Hu tieu
summary: Hủ tiếu is a clear, delicate, slightly sweet broth, the bowl that belongs in this city while phở belongs in Hanoi. Nam Vang uses thin rice noodles and Sa Đéc a chewier noodle with a sweet Delta sauce, and the Nam Vang toppings differ: shrimp, pork, quail eggs, and fried garlic; or boiled eggs, shrimp, and pork as ground meat, lean meat, liver, intestines, and tongue; or prawn, minced pork, pork intestines, and quail eggs with fried garlic and raw vegetables.
origin: Vietnam Tourism says few dishes represent the city as this one does, with Chinese, Cambodian, and Vietnamese origins. Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is a different bowl.
history: The local-eating page traces hủ tiếu Nam Vang to Chinese, Cambodian, and Vietnamese cooking, and hủ tiếu Sa Đéc to the former Sa Đéc province.
culture: The cuisine page says phở gets the acclaim and hủ tiếu is the bowl to eat here. Nam Vang, that other page says, is on carts all over the city.
texture: Sa Đéc, on the local-eating page, has a chewier noodle than the Nam Vang bowl. The cuisine page says the dry bowl comes with the broth on the side.
taste: The cuisine account calls the broth delicate, slightly sweet, and clear. Sa Đéc comes with a sweet sauce called a Delta signature. Both descriptions stay.
howToEat: Nam Vang, on the local-eating page: thin rice noodles in a hot bone broth, shrimp, pork, quail eggs, and fried garlic.
Sa Đéc: a chewier noodle, the sweet sauce, and a plate of bean sprouts and lettuce.

The cuisine page’s broth is simmered with pork bones, dried squid, shrimp, and root vegetables, topped with boiled eggs, shrimp, and pork as ground meat, lean meat, liver, intestines, and tongue. Add lettuce, bean sprouts, and scallions. The photograph is a Nam Vang bowl: noodles, pork, minced pork, fried shallot, chili, and lime.

The delicious-dishes page’s Nam Vang bowl is soft, chewy rice noodles made from rice flour, in a rich broth with prawn, minced pork, pork intestines, and quail eggs, with fried garlic and raw vegetables. That topping list is not the same as the two above.
where: Carts across the city. Hủ tiếu Ba Hoàng is at 56 Võ Văn Tần, District 3. Hủ tiếu Mỹ Tho is a different dish.
seoTitle: Hủ tiếu in Ho Chi Minh City
seoDescription: Nam Vang and Sa Đéc hủ tiếu in Ho Chi Minh City, and the broth the national cuisine page describes. Not the Mỹ Tho bowl, and not phở.
